verified_claim_families: The 1m composite DTM is a raster elevation model covering approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM represents terrain after surface objects are removed from the DSM using automated methods and manual editing.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest and best-resolution data is selected.
Resampled data uses bilinear interpolation before merging.
The cited composite period spans 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
Metadata index catalogues identify the survey used at a location.
Composite downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevation values are in metres and referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The composite uses the OSTN15 transformation method and EPSG:27700 horizontal coordinates.
Individual surveys contributing to the composite are described with vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
Time-stamped DTM tiles are available at multiple resolutions and preserve survey-specific dates, transformations and geoid models in metadata.
All public survey data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
Post-26 August 2016 surveys use the OSGM15 geoid model; earlier surveys require metadata-specific geoid handling.
WMS is for visualised elevation while WCS is the numeric coverage service, so numeric promotion must use coverage bytes rather than map imagery.
Exact TQ2892 filtered metadata, WCS response bytes and candidate-specific numeric cell values were not read back in this runtime.
